typography-as-brand-voice.prior: treat type as the primary identity carrier, so distinctive faces and expressive contrast do the branding work themselves

meaning-first-color.prior: Color should encode meaning and identity rather than decorate, so every hue maps to a concept, state, or accent that communicates intent.

airy-minimalism.prior: prioritize open space and lightweight layering so content breathes and feels effortless, unconstrained, and premium

always-alive-presence.prior: An interface should feel perpetually alive and present, signaling ongoing activity through subtle continuous motion rather than appearing static or dormant.

depth-through-light-not-lines.prior: Convey hierarchy and elevation by simulating how light, shadow, and translucency behave in physical space rather than using explicit borders or dividers.

tactile-realism.prior: surfaces should evoke physical material presence so interfaces feel believable and touchable

friction-over-freedom.prior: When users try to disengage, keep them nominally in control while raising the cost of exit—so retention is preserved without an explicit block.

information-dense-command-center.prior: Center a primary focus and layer synchronized secondary views around it so users can monitor and act on complex state at a glance.

moves.entity-driven-color: --entity-air:#4da8ff and --entity-ground:#b07bff distinguish subject categories (air vs ground); usage 'background: signal.hue' / 'color: signal.hue' binds color to the entity being rendered
moves.semantic-status-color: --signal-live:#34e0a1, --signal-warn:#ffcf5c, --signal-crit:#ff4d6d encode operational state, reinforced by .presence beacon-pulse as a 'live presence signal'
moves.expressive-accent: --accent:#ff4d1f / --accent-hot:#ff7a3d bold saturated orange as identity, bleeding into elevation: .elev-dramatic uses '0 24px 64px -16px rgba(255,77,31,0.2)'
moves.restrained-neutral-chrome: layered near-black neutrals --ground/#080b12 through --surface-2/#1b2233 with muted --text-mid/--text-dim ground the expressive signal/entity hues; comment 'dramatic float — NEUTRAL ink (hue lives on marking)'

application.evidence: --ground #080b12 sets body background; dark canvas is the base
--surface-0/1/2 build cards/panels (BeaconCard, DetailPanel bg var(--surface-2)) via the lit gradient object
--text-hi/mid/dim carry all copy across BeaconCanvas, BeaconCard, DetailPanel
shadows/bevels are neutral ink — 'dramatic float — NEUTRAL ink (hue lives on marking)', rgba(0,0,0) elevation, glass rgba(13,17,25)
--accent #ff4d1f used as color:var(--accent) to light the focal beacon marking in BeaconCanvas
elev-dramatic adds a warm glow 0 24px 64px rgba(255,77,31,0.2) — accent bleeds into elevation atmosphere
signal-live/warn/crit and entity-air/ground only ever appear as signal.hue on beacon dots, badge fills and status labels in BeaconCard/DetailPanel

_checklist: COMPOSITION — organize around a central-canvas spine.  WHY: Center a primary focus and layer synchronized secondary views around it so users can monitor and act on complex state at a glance.

TYPOGRAPHY — carry the moves ['custom-display-face', 'distinct-body-face', 'expressive-weight', 'extreme-scale-contrast', 'treated-microtype', 'type-as-graphic'].  WHY: treat type as the primary identity carrier.

COLOR — carry the moves ['entity-driven-color', 'expressive-accent', 'semantic-status-color'] · APPLICATION: keep ['semantic'] color to marking (data/text/interactive), never flood it onto surfaces · ground is DARK (tonality 0.08) — match that polarity.  WHY: Color should encode meaning and identity rather than decorate.

DENSITY — carry the moves ['floating-overlays', 'full-bleed-canvas', 'generous-hero-space'].  WHY: prioritize open space and lightweight layering so content breathes and feels effortless, unconstrained, and premium.

AMBIENT — carry the moves ['breathing-pulse', 'drift-scroll', 'perpetual-loop', 'presence-signal', 'rotation-spin'].  WHY: An interface should feel perpetually alive and present, signaling ongoing activity through subtle continuous motion rather than appearing static or dormant.

ELEVATION — carry the moves ['backdrop-blur', 'colored-shadow', 'dramatic-shadow', 'inset-depth', 'layered-overlays', 'soft-floating-shadows'].  WHY: Convey hierarchy and elevation by simulating how light, shadow, and translucency behave in physical space rather than using explicit borders or dividers.

SURFACE/focal-entity — a materially-rich focal object (layers ['bevel', 'lighting', 'sheen', 'texture']).  WHY: surfaces should evoke physical material presence so interfaces feel believable and touchable.

BEHAVIOR/reveal — an interaction carrying ['demote-not-remove', 'interaction-lock', 'manufactured-latency', 'multi-phase'].  WHY: When users try to disengage, keep them nominally in control while raising the cost of exit—so retention is preserved without an explicit block.

BEHAVIOR/rest — an interaction carrying ['demote-not-remove', 'interaction-lock', 'manufactured-latency', 'multi-phase'].  WHY: When users try to disengage, keep them nominally in control while raising the cost of exit—so retention is preserved without an explicit block.

BEHAVIOR/toggle — an interaction carrying ['demote-not-remove', 'interaction-lock', 'manufactured-latency', 'multi-phase'].  WHY: When users try to disengage, keep them nominally in control while raising the cost of exit—so retention is preserved without an explicit block.

COMPONENT/beacon-card — Build a component that expands attached to its trigger (a dropdown/disclosure), carrying material [bevel, lighting, sheen, texture] and hosting interaction [demote-not-remove, interaction-lock, manufactured-latency, multi-phase] — combine the aesthetic and the interaction in the SAME object.

_guide.build_to_the_why: The checklist's WHY clauses are the product's dispositions — its soul. Build to those principles, not just to pass the checks. A check is a floor, not the finish: passing conformance means you didn't violate the grammar, NOT that it feels like one designer's hand.
build_order: 1. SKELETON — stand up the composition spine and the focal object first (structure before style). A great skin on no spine reads as generic.
2. MATERIAL — give the focal object its layered material (the SURFACE moves).
3. BEHAVIOR — bind the interaction grammar (gesture → response) on the component roles.
4. STYLE — carry each facet's moves at the stated MAGNITUDE (as loud as the source, not a tasteful echo).
5. POLISH — the craft below. This is where a passing build becomes a good one.

you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.note: Static analysis reads declared DOM/CSS, not the rendered/animated result. These are real identity but UNVERIFIABLE — a green report does NOT cover them, so they are yours to get right by hand.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.motion_smoothness: Real easing and staged timing — no linear tweens, no jank. Animate transform/opacity, not layout. Honor prefers-reduced-motion.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.color_harmony: The palette must read as ONE system — even lightness/chroma steps, restrained hue families. Passing the color moves ≠ a harmonious palette.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.type_layout: Clean arrangement — aligned to a grid, consistent vertical rhythm, a hierarchy that reads. (Rich size vocabularies are fine; sloppy ARRANGEMENT is not.)
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.material_feel: Glossy vs flat, focal richness — the rendered richness the layer/alpha counts can't distinguish. Make the focal object look genuinely lit.

_guide.reading_the_gate: The gate is DETERMINISTIC except color, which is semantic (marking-vs-decoration is a judgment about meaning). Consequences: (a) a FAIL that stays IDENTICAL on UNCHANGED code is REAL — fix the build, do not re-run hoping it clears, and do not contort code to game a signature. (b) The color check can shift between edits because it re-reads meaning; trust a stable verdict on unchanged code. (c) 'accent decorates instead of marks' is about MEANING: a colored glow on a data entity MARKS (good); a decorative gradient DECORATES (flagged).
